ui.menu.foot: Sixty days until the spring steamship. Will you live to see it?
ui.about.title: ABOUT
ui.about.p1: An isometric survival game in the spirit of Project Zomboid: the Russian North, November 1917. The revolution has swept the country, and only a rumour has reached your trading post — the spring steamship is sixty days away.
ui.about.p2: Search for food and fuel, keep the stoves burning, set snares for hare, sew valenki out of hides, read other people’s letters. The wolves are hungry this winter — and so are the deserters. Death is final: the save is destroyed.

item.podshlemnin.name: Podshlemnik knit hood
item.podshlemnin.desc: A knitted hood for the whole head: ears, nape, brow. Meant to go under a cap — and without a cap you won’t last a week.
item.kartuz.name: Kartuz peaked cap
item.kartuz.desc: A townsman’s kartuz with a lacquered peak. Good for winter — as far as the store and back.
item.platok.name: Woman’s wool shawl
item.platok.desc: A heavy wool shawl in big roses. Knotted under the chin, the ends crossed behind.
item.kapor.name: Woman’s bonnet
item.kapor.desc: A broadcloth bonnet with fur trim. Tied under the chin; brow and cheeks stay covered.
item.bashlyk.name: Bashlyk
item.bashlyk.desc: A pointy hood with long ends: wind them round your neck — and the blizzard stays outside.
item.shlyapa_fetrovaya.name: Felt hat
item.shlyapa_fetrovaya.desc: A town felt hat with a band. Good for reading newspapers in — and that’s all.
item.bogatyrka.name: Bogatyrka fur cap
item.bogatyrka.desc: A tall fur cap with a cloth crown. The sheepskin has gone shaggy, but your head is as warm as in a stove.
item.ushanka_barin.name: Gentleman’s ushanka
item.ushanka_barin.desc: Karakul over beaver fur, a velvet top, silk ties. Gentry begins with heads like this.
item.malakhai.name: Malakhai
item.malakhai.desc: A hunter’s cap of reindeer leg-hide: earflaps, a nape flap, fur laid against the nap. Hoar-frost does not settle on it.
item.shlem_soldatsky.name: Soldier’s helmet
item.shlem_soldatsky.desc: A stamped steel helmet with a broadcloth lining. It holds the head together; it does not spoil it with warmth.
item.rubakha_natelnaya.name: Next-to-skin shirt
item.rubakha_natelnaya.desc: Hempen, to the knees, no collar — just a slit. The thing you don’t take off for weeks.
item.rubakha_ispodnyaya.name: Woollen undershirt
item.rubakha_ispodnyaya.desc: A woollen undershirt, darned the thrifty way. It itches, but it is warm.
item.kosovorotka.name: Kosovorotka shirt
item.kosovorotka.desc: A shirt with a side collar and red trim. Good at the table in it — and only at the table.
item.gimnastyorka.name: Gymnastyorka
item.gimnastyorka.desc: A soldier’s broadcloth jacket on hooks. The shoulder straps were picked off — the owner’s year was not an easy one.
item.sviter_gruboy.name: Coarse-knit sweater
item.sviter_gruboy.desc: Sheep’s wool a finger thick; smells of smoke and the sheep-shed. Knitted by somebody’s mother, long ago.
item.sviter_rybiy.name: Fish-oil sweater
item.sviter_rybiy.desc: Pomor yarn steeped in cod-liver oil. It shines and it stinks — and even soaked, it keeps the cold out.
item.tuzhurka.name: Tuzhurka uniform jacket
item.tuzhurka.desc: A clerk’s uniform jacket: broadcloth, tin buttons, ink stains on the right cuff.
item.pidzhak_stary.name: Worn jacket
item.pidzhak_stary.desc: Three buttons out of four, the elbows shining. Half the district runs on such things — poverty and invention.
item.chuika.name: Chuyka
item.chuika.desc: A long broadcloth kaftan on hooks. Deaf as an Old Believer: the wind won’t get in — and neither will the warmth.
item.palto_drapovoe.name: Heavy wool coat
item.palto_drapovoe.desc: Town broadcloth in two layers, little bun-shaped buttons. Wet snow rolls off it; hard frost does not.
item.poddevka.name: Wadded jacket
item.poddevka.desc: Quilted over wadding: between the rows of wadding there is air — and air is what warmth is.
item.zhilet_mekhovoy.name: Fur waistcoat
item.zhilet_mekhovoy.desc: Sheepskin worn hide-out, no sleeves. The chest stays warm — freeze your arms off yourself, if you like.
item.smoking.name: Dress suit
item.smoking.desc: Black, with satin lapels. Useless in the taiga — but bandits value it by the weight of bread.
item.fartuk_kozhany.name: Leather apron
item.fartuk_kozhany.desc: A smith’s apron: sparks glance off, damp doesn’t take. Let it shine — no harm to the work.
item.shinel.name: Greatcoat
item.shinel.desc: Grey army broadcloth to the heels. The smoke of war, lice, and four kilos — but under it, it’s like an izba.
item.shinel_avstriyskaya.name: Austrian greatcoat
item.shinel_avstriyskaya.desc: A trophy from Galicia: cloth denser than the Russian kind, bone buttons. Front-line men gave a lot for one of these.
item.armyak.name: Armyak
item.armyak.desc: A long coachman’s kaftan worn over everything. It dislikes runners — it loves the road and patience.
item.bekesha.name: Bekesha
item.bekesha.desc: A fur coat covered in broadcloth: fur inside, cloth out. It doesn’t soak and doesn’t stink — a well-off man’s thing.
item.polushubok.name: Half-length fur coat
item.polushubok.desc: A sheepskin coat to the knees: the warmth of half a tulup — and the weight of one too. A working winter thing.
item.tulup_ovchinniy.name: Sheepskin tulup
item.tulup_ovchinniy.desc: Worn hide-out, to the heels, fur within. A Russian stove on your shoulders — if you don’t count the smell of mutton.
item.tulup_volchiy.name: Wolf-fur tulup
item.tulup_volchiy.desc: Four wolf hides sewn with sinew. The fur moves in waves in the wind — and the wolf is cold no longer, and neither are you.
item.portki_ispodnie.name: Under-breeches
item.portki_ispodnie.desc: Hempen, worn under the trousers. Little good in them — but bare legs on the frost are a surer ruin than the wolf.
item.kalsony.name: Warm long johns
item.kalsony.desc: Flannel, with ties at the ankles. Town undergarments — remarkably dependable warmth.
item.shtany_holshovye.name: Hempen trousers
item.shtany_holshovye.desc: Work trousers of hemp canvas. They hold up nothing but the owner’s dignity.
item.sharovary.name: Sharovary trousers
item.sharovary.desc: Wide ones — three fathoms of cloth to a pair. The fabric bellies out and keeps the wind outside: a stove of air.
item.bryuki_gorodskie.name: Town trousers
item.bryuki_gorodskie.desc: Broadcloth, striped, pressed once upon a time. Decent legs — half of decency.
item.poneva.name: Poneva skirt
item.poneva.desc: The checked skirt of a married peasant woman: broadcloth, a sash with a tassel. It holds warmth the woman’s way — with its hem.
item.shtany_vatnye.name: Wadded trousers
item.shtany_vatnye.desc: Quilted, two handfuls of wadding apiece. Without them a carter turns into a monument to himself by evening.
item.portki_mekhovye.name: Fur breeches
item.portki_mekhovye.desc: Fur side in, on drawstrings. At winter hunting camps they are currency, salvation and blanket all at once.
item.lapti.name: Lapti bast shoes
item.lapti.desc: Bast, with bindings over the heel. You won’t keep your feet in them for long — but to the barefoot, lapti are footwear too.
item.chuni.name: Rag-knit house shoes
item.chuni.desc: Little boots knitted of rags. House footwear — in them you go no farther than the woodpile.
item.porshni.name: Porshni
item.porshni.desc: Leather soles with a strap: one piece of hide, an awl, and wit. Footwear as old as the North.
item.galoshi.name: Galoshes
item.galoshi.desc: Rubber, worn over the valenki. In a thaw — salvation; in frost — slippery and foolish.
item.boty_gorodskie.name: Leather button boots
item.boty_gorodskie.desc: Town ones, on buttons, the heels run down. Decent on floorboards — torment on snow.
item.sapogi_kirzovye.name: Kirza boots
item.sapogi_kirzovye.desc: State-issue coarse leather, creaking across the whole settlement. They don’t soak — and they drown in drifts up to the top.
item.sapogi_yalovye.name: Calfskin boots
item.sapogi_yalovye.desc: Soft calfskin, tar in the seams. Drier than kirza in a thaw — and thrice the price.
item.valenki_vysokie.name: Tall felt valenki
item.valenki_vysokie.desc: Rolled felt to the knee: in hard frost — a stove on your legs; in a thaw — a sponge. They walk on the crust on top.
item.unty.name: Unty fur boots
item.unty.desc: Reindeer, of leg-hide, fur outside. In a blizzard your feet feel no cold — if the unty are yours, and not taken off someone.
item.varezhki_holshovye.name: Canvas work mitts
item.varezhki_holshovye.desc: Work mitts: hands safe from splinters — the frost finds the chinks on its own.
item.mitenki.name: Knitted fingerless mitts
item.mitenki.desc: Fingers free: seat a cartridge, tie a knot. Shooting is easier in these.
item.perchatki_kozhanye.name: Leather gloves
item.perchatki_kozhanye.desc: Thin leather, a cord at the wrist. The trigger obeys the fingers — the frost obeys no one, least of all them.
item.rukavitsy_ovchinnye.name: Sheepskin mittens
item.rukavitsy_ovchinnye.desc: Fur side in, and a thumb to drive a nail. A grandfather’s answer to the frost: “and who might you be?”
item.rukavitsy_volchi.name: Wolf-fur mittens
item.rukavitsy_volchi.desc: From the paws of an old wolf: grey fur, a black ridge. Hands the wolf will no longer freeze.
item.shal.name: Shawl
item.shal.desc: A big wool one, in scrollwork patterns. It smells of naphthalene and someone’s kind word.
item.nakidka.name: Broadcloth cape
item.nakidka.desc: A tarred cape pulled over the head; the wind holds the flaps. Wet blizzard rolls off it.
item.kotomka.name: Bast shoulder pack
item.kotomka.desc: A birch-bark box on the back, with bast straps. The throat takes anything — the back endures.
item.meshok_ohotnika.name: Hunter’s sack
item.meshok_ohotnika.desc: Canvas, a strap, loops for the ice chisel. A whole beast fits inside — together with its smell for the whole neighbourhood.
item.ranets.name: Soldier’s pack
item.ranets.desc: Canvas and leather, the pack buckles shining. Inside — a trace of someone else’s padded jacket and a scrap of a letter.
item.zipun.name: Zipun
item.zipun.desc: A coarse kaftan flung anyhow over the shoulders. It smells of smoke, tar and mutton flank — a peasant’s salvation.
item.skatka.name: Greatcoat roll
item.skatka.desc: Grey broadcloth rolled into a length over the shoulder. The regulations died — the blanket and the pillow remained.
item.mundir_telegrafa.name: Telegraph operator’s uniform
item.mundir_telegrafa.desc: Double-breasted, brass buttons, ink-stitching in the lining: “St. Beloye, 1914.”
item.kitel_feldshera.name: Feldsher’s shabby tunic
item.kitel_feldshera.desc: A worn lapel, the smell of carbolic. Its little pocket remembers the medicine lists — and medicines turn up more willingly.
item.sviter_very.name: Vera’s sweater
item.sviter_very.desc: Blue snowflakes along the hem, sleeves longer than the hands. Knitted for a brother who never came back from the Oka.
item.ryasa_diakona.name: Deacon’s cassock
item.ryasa_diakona.desc: Black, heavy, in wax and incense. Sins roll off shoulders like these of their own accord.
item.shinel_dezertira.name: Deserter’s greatcoat
item.shinel_dezertira.desc: State broadcloth, someone else’s blood on the shoulder. In the ripped lining — a rusk and a medal “For Diligence”.
item.polushubok_timofeicha.name: Timofeich’s half-length fur coat
item.polushubok_timofeicha.desc: Seven winters of sheepskin, a sable patch on the collar. The forest knows this sheepskin, and shows its tracks.
item.furazhka_nachalnika.name: Stationmaster’s peaked cap
item.furazhka_nachalnika.desc: A polished crown, a cracked band, finger marks on the peak: the timetable waits its hour.
item.shuba_balakirevoy.name: Merchant Balakireva’s fur coat
item.shuba_balakirevoy.desc: Black-brown fox on squirrel lining, a sable collar. Forty degrees below is a laugh to it; the weight — a telegraph pole.
item.treukh_garmonista.name: Harmonist’s treukh
item.treukh_garmonista.desc: A hare-fur treukh with a dented crown: “Moonlight” has been played under it for thirty years. Longing retreats.
item.doha_pastukha.name: Shepherd’s doha
item.doha_pastukha.desc: Fur side out, a hood with a fox edging. Forty years of someone else’s herd — and the snow rolls off it.

amb.ice.sings: The river ice creaks and sings.
amb.dogs.first: Somewhere in the village dogs are barking. So there is still life there.
amb.bells.first: Sunday bells drift from the belfry. Somewhere, a service goes on.
amb.fox.first: An orange spark at the forest edge. A fox.
amb.track: Old wolf tracks, half-buried in snow.
amb.atmo.silence: The silence is so deep you can hear the blood in your ears.
amb.atmo.snowhurries: The snow falls as if it is in a hurry to get somewhere.
amb.atmo.nobirds: Not a single bird in the sky.
amb.atmo.fern: The frost paints ferns on the window glass.
amb.atmo.pillar: The chimney smoke stands straight — a hard night is coming.
amb.atmo.leaden: The sky is heavy, leaden — pressing on the shoulders.
amb.atmo.creek: Somewhere under the snow a brook still murmurs.
w2.inei.start: Hoarfrost fell. The world grew a shade lighter.
w2.izm.start: Rime: the trees donned white fur.
w2.ice.start: Freezing rain! Everything grows a crust of ice.
w2.ice.end: The rain is over. All is crusted in ice — slippery.
w2.ice.fall: Your feet slid out on the ice!
w2.groza.name: Thundersnow
w2.groza.first: A thundersnow! Lightning tears the white murk.
w2.wo.name: White wall
w2.wo.start: A white wall. Cannot see an outstretched hand.
w2.wo.end_lost: The wall has passed, but where you are — not so clear now.
w2.ice.name: Freezing rain
w2.halo.start: A rainbow ring around the sun. A hard frost is coming.
w2.moonhalo.start: A pale ring around the moon. A hard frost is coming.
w2.parost.start: Frost mist hangs above the river.
w2.clim.soft: November is mild: the snow lies, the frost still dozes.
w2.clim.dec: December sets in — the frost grips your sides.
w2.clim.deep: The frosts grow harder. Epiphany will be fierce.
w2.clim.epiphany: Epiphany cold. So cold the air rings.
w2.clim.relax: The cold loosens its grip, a little.
w2.clim.end: The frost retreats. Soon the steamboat will come up the river.

item.shchi.name: Shchi (Cabbage Soup)
item.shchi.desc: Fresh cabbage, potatoes, onion: a full pot of dinner.
item.shchi_sour.name: Sour Shchi
item.shchi_sour.desc: Sauerkraut and salt pork: sourness that suits the palate.
item.borscht.name: Borscht
item.borscht.desc: Beets, cabbage, potatoes and meat: a rich crimson broth.
item.ukha_fish.name: Ukha (Fish Soup)
item.ukha_fish.desc: Two fish and an onion — and don't say that's not a broth.
item.ukha_double.name: Double Ukha
item.ukha_double.desc: Broth from one catch, fish from another: a Pomor's cunning.
item.ukha_milk.name: Milk Ukha
item.ukha_milk.desc: Fish simmered in milk: White Sea tenderness.
item.kalya.name: Kalya (Fish Soup)
item.kalya.desc: Fish with pickled cucumbers and pearl barley: an age-old soup.
item.rassolnik.name: Rassolnik
item.rassolnik.desc: Pearl barley and pickles: the tang cures hangover and gloom.
item.solyanka.name: Meat Solyanka
item.solyanka.desc: Meat, cucumber, onion: thick enough to sink a spoon.
item.solyanka_fish.name: Fish Solyanka
item.solyanka_fish.desc: Salted fish and pickles: a soup with character.
item.mushroom_soup.name: Gribovnitsa (Mushroom Soup)
item.mushroom_soup.desc: Mushroom broth with potatoes: the forest in a spoon.
item.pea_soup.name: Pea Soup
item.pea_soup.desc: Peas, potatoes, onion: filling and cheap.
item.nettle_soup.name: Nettle Soup
item.nettle_soup.desc: Young nettles in broth: the scurvy retreats.
item.kholodets.name: Kholodets (Meat Aspic)
item.kholodets.desc: Bones, meat and patience: once it sets, cut it with a knife.
item.kholodets_fish.name: Fish Kholodets
item.kholodets_fish.desc: Fish jelly with onion: quivers like a northern lake.
item.lapsha_soup.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
item.lapsha_soup.desc: Homemade hand-cut noodles in chicken broth.
item.broth_chicken.name: Chicken Broth
item.broth_chicken.desc: A clear broth: drink it hot, and the sick one drinks first.
item.kasha_buckwheat.name: Buckwheat Kasha
item.kasha_buckwheat.desc: Groats in water: with a bit of onion, no tsar ate better.
item.kasha_millet.name: Millet Kasha
item.kasha_millet.desc: Millet boiled soft: a child's joy and a grown man's dinner.
item.kasha_oat.name: Oat Kasha
item.kasha_oat.desc: Porridge oats cooked down to tenderness.
item.kasha_semolina.name: Semolina Kasha
item.kasha_semolina.desc: Semolina in milk with butter: the way grandmother made it.
item.kasha_pea.name: Pea Kasha
item.kasha_pea.desc: Mashed peas: heartier than meat, so the old men say.
item.kasha_barley.name: Barley Kasha
item.kasha_barley.desc: Pearl barley with butter: grinds on the teeth, sticks to the ribs.
item.kasha_pumpkin.name: Pumpkin Kasha
item.kasha_pumpkin.desc: Millet and pumpkin in milk: a sweet dinner.
item.kasha_milk.name: Milk Kasha
item.kasha_milk.desc: Kasha cooked in whole milk: two full pots.
item.polevaya_kasha.name: Field Kasha
item.polevaya_kasha.desc: Groats, salt pork and onion: the artel's communal pot.
item.kasha_grib.name: Buckwheat with Mushrooms
item.kasha_grib.desc: Groats with dried mushrooms and onion: Lent holds no fear.
item.tolokno.name: Tolokno (Oat Flour)
item.tolokno.desc: Oat flour stirred with milk: eat with a spoon and hit the road.
item.meat_stew.name: Home-Canned Meat Stew
item.meat_stew.desc: Meat in its own fat: the jar will keep till spring.
item.fish_stew.name: Stewed Fish
item.fish_stew.desc: Fish slow-simmered with potato and onion.
item.pelmeni_boiled.name: Pelmeni, Boiled
item.pelmeni_boiled.desc: Boiled in bubbling water: with vinegar and pepper.
item.potato_baked.name: Ash-Baked Potatoes
item.potato_baked.desc: Baked in embers: scalds the fingers, warms the gut.
item.potato_mashed.name: Mashed Potatoes
item.potato_mashed.desc: Potatoes mashed with butter: a mound and a spoon.
item.cabbage_stewed.name: Stewed Cabbage
item.cabbage_stewed.desc: Cabbage simmered with onion: a side, or a meal in itself.
item.kotlety.name: Cutlets
item.kotlety.desc: Minced meat patties with a crisp crust.
item.kotlety_fish.name: Fish Cutlets
item.kotlety_fish.desc: Fish patties: bones picked out, mince well beaten.
item.kotlety_chicken.name: Chicken Cutlets
item.kotlety_chicken.desc: Chicken with egg and bread: melts in the mouth.
item.kotlety_mushroom.name: Mushroom Cutlets
item.kotlety_mushroom.desc: Mushrooms, bread and onion: a lenten stand-in for meat.
item.chops_hare.name: Hare Cutlets
item.chops_hare.desc: Game meat with lard: a hunter's lunch.
item.giblets_stew.name: Stewed Giblets
item.giblets_stew.desc: Heart and liver with onion: poor fare, but tasty.
item.befstrogan.name: Beef Stroganoff
item.befstrogan.desc: Strips of meat in sour cream and onion: a general's dinner.
item.bear_paw_jellied.name: Jellied Bear Paw
item.bear_paw_jellied.desc: A tsar's dish: bear's strength in aspic. Sanity +15
item.roasted_hare.name: Roast Hare
item.roast_chicken.name: Roast Chicken
item.roast_chicken.desc: Bird fried in lard: golden, with a crackle.
item.draniki.name: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
item.draniki.desc: Grated potato with egg: grand with cracklings.
item.fish_fried.name: Fried Fish
item.fish_fried.desc: Rolled in flour and fried to a golden hue.
item.fish_smoked.name: Smoked Fish
item.fish_smoked.desc: Hot-smoked: the smoke keeps it and flavors it.
item.mushrooms_fried.name: Fried Mushrooms
item.mushrooms_fried.desc: Forest meat from the frying pan.
item.mushroom_caviar.name: Mushroom Caviar
item.mushroom_caviar.desc: Chopped mushrooms with onion: spread it on bread.
item.mushroom_potato.name: Potatoes with Mushrooms
item.mushroom_potato.desc: Mushrooms and potatoes in a cast-iron pot: a lenten supper.
item.potato_salo.name: Potatoes with Salo
item.potato_salo.desc: The salo renders, the potatoes brown.
item.egg_boiled.name: Hard-Boiled Eggs
item.egg_boiled.desc: Boiled hard: pocket one for the road.
item.egg_fried.name: Fried Eggs
item.egg_fried.desc: Fried in butter: the edges go crisp.
item.beet_baked.name: Baked Beet
item.turnip_stewed.name: Steamed Turnip
item.turnip_stewed.desc: Turnip slow-steamed in the stove: a grandfather's dinner.
item.dough_rich.name: Rich Dough
item.dough_rich.desc: Flour, egg and milk: for blini and oladji.
item.bread_rye_black.name: Rye Bread, Black
item.bread_rye_black.desc: Black, sourdough: one loaf lasts the week.
item.bread_white.name: White Bread
item.bread_white.desc: A wheat loaf: soft, good with tea.
item.karavay.name: Karavai (Round Loaf)
item.karavay.desc: “Karavai, karavai, choose the one you love.” Sanity +8
item.kulich.name: Kulich (Easter Bread)
item.kulich.desc: Easter sweet bread: a bright and holy thing. Sanity +10
item.blini.name: Blini (Pancakes)
item.blini.desc: Thin and lacy: with sour cream and honey.
item.blini_buckwheat.name: Buckwheat Blini
item.oladji.name: Oladji (Thick Pancakes)
item.pirozhki.name: Meat Pirozhki
item.pirozhki.desc: Soft, meat-filled: one is enough to fill you.
item.pirozhki_fish.name: Fish Pirozhki
item.pirozhki_fish.desc: Fish in dough: a Pomor's pocketful.
item.pirozhki_cabbage.name: Cabbage Pirozhki
item.pirozhki_cabbage.desc: Cabbage with onion: cheap and heartwarming.
item.pirozhki_mushroom.name: Mushroom Pirozhki
item.pirozhki_mushroom.desc: Mushroom filling: the forest in your pocket.
item.pirog_cabbage.name: Cabbage Pirog
item.pirog_cabbage.desc: A broad, generous pie: cut it for the whole family.
item.pirog_fish.name: Rybnik (Fish Pie)
item.pirog_fish.desc: A whole fish in dough: northern wealth.
item.shangi.name: Shangi (Siberian Buns)
item.shangi.desc: Little suns topped with potato and butter.
item.rasskezhi.name: Rasskezhi (Open Pies)
item.rasskezhi.desc: Open boat-shapes with fish: tavern classics.
item.sochniki.name: Sochniki (Curd Pastries)
item.sochniki.desc: Rich dough folds with a curd middle.
item.vatrushka.name: Vatrushka (Curd Bun)
item.vatrushka.desc: A tender curd heart in a soft rim of dough.
item.pryanik.name: Mint Pryanik
item.pryanik.desc: A stamped gingerbread: soft, with a mint soul.
item.sushki.name: Sushki (Bread Rings)
item.sushki.desc: Crunchy little rings: soak them a week, and they’re food again.
item.baranki.name: Baranki (Dough Rings)
item.baranki.desc: Rich dough rings: hard, but good-hearted.
item.suhari.name: Army Rusks
item.suhari.desc: Sliced and dried: field rations for any road.
item.tart_berries.name: Berry Yatka
item.tart_berries.desc: An open pie of lingonberries: a tart-sweet edge.
item.pastila.name: Pastila (Apple Sweet)
item.mushrooms_pickled.name: Pickled Mushrooms
item.mushrooms_pickled.desc: In a strong brine: they’ll keep till Easter.
item.mushrooms_salted.name: Salted Mushrooms
item.mushrooms_salted.desc: Milk mushrooms and more: just the thing with boiled potatoes.
item.cabbage_sauer_full.name: Barrel of Sauerkraut
item.cabbage_sauer_full.desc: A full cask: vitamins for the whole winter.
item.fish_dried_hang.name: Dried Yukola
item.fish_dried_hang.desc: Hung up and dried whole: provisions for the road.
item.meat_jerky.name: Dried Meat
item.meat_jerky.desc: Salted strips of meat: it crunches, and it feeds.
item.meat_smoked.name: Smoked Meat
item.meat_smoked.desc: Dipped in smoke — it came out of the stove ready to eat.
item.salo_salted.name: Salo (Salted Lard)
item.salo_salted.desc: A slab salted to the bone: if only for some garlic…
item.vinegret.name: Vinegret (Beet Salad)
item.vinegret.desc: The beets have stained it all crimson: a Lenten salad.
item.berries_mors.name: Mors (Berry Drink)
item.berries_mors.desc: Lingonberry mors: makes a sour life sweeter.
item.kissel.name: Kissel (Berry Pudding)
item.kissel.desc: Berry kissel: thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
item.kissel_oat.name: Oat Kissel
item.kissel_oat.desc: Drink and meal in one: for babes and old men.
item.compote_dried.name: Mixed Compote
item.compote_dried.desc: Dried fruit and berries in sugar: summer in a mug.
item.tea_ivan.name: Koporye Tea
item.tea_ivan.desc: Fireweed tea: dark, fragrant, none of that overseas bitterness.
item.tea_chaga_brew.name: Brewed Chaga
item.tea_chaga_brew.desc: A dark chaga brew: drives off illness and warms the gut.
item.tea_pine.name: Pine Needle Tea
item.tea_pine.desc: Needles with sugar: bitter, but the scurvy retreats.
item.sbiten.name: Sbiten (Hot Honey Drink)
item.sbiten.desc: Honey, boiling water, a touch of sugar — warms you from within. Sanity +6
item.varenets.name: Varenets (Baked Milk)
item.varenets.desc: Baked milk soured with cream: a Siberian supper.
item.pryanik_honey.name: Honey Pryanik
item.pryanik_honey.desc: Made with pure honey: for tea from the samovar.
item.prianik_honey.name: Pryanik, Honey
item.prianik_honey.desc: Same honey, same spice — just written differently.
item.medovik.name: Medovik (Honey Cake)
item.medovik.desc: A merchant’s cake: eight layers with sour cream. Sanity +10
item.pascha.name: Curd Paskha
item.pascha.desc: A mountain of curd with raisins (the raisins only in dreams). Sanity +12
item.syrniki.name: Syrniki (Curd Fritters)
item.relic_icon_kazan.name: Kazan Icon in a Kiot
item.relic_icon_kazan.desc: Silver oklad, scratched by bayonet or claw. The faith is whole. (Church, altar)
item.relic_bell_small.name: Blagovest Hand Bell
item.relic_bell_small.desc: Cast by a Vologda master, 1889. A pure ring, heard a verst away. (Church, candle stand)
item.relic_gospel.name: Gospel in Velvet
item.relic_gospel.desc: Silver-gilt darkened; letters clear. “Gift of merchant Balakirev.” (Church, lectern)
item.relic_teapot_silver.name: Silver Teapot, Merchant’s
item.relic_teapot_silver.desc: The crest on the lid is nailed over — hastily, with feeling. (The Balakirevs’ dacha)
item.relic_watch_chain.name: Ship’s Chronometer
item.relic_watch_chain.desc: Engraved “St. Nicholas, 1903.” Navigator’s piece; keeps time. (Station, telegraph pole)
item.relic_telegraph_key.name: Telegraph Key, Brass
item.relic_telegraph_key.desc: Worn to a shine. No counting the words that passed through it. (Station, telegraph room)
item.relic_karavai_blessed.name: Dried-Out Prosphora
item.relic_karavai_blessed.desc: Dried hard as stone. Kept in linen, given in remembrance. (Church, tabernacle)
item.relic_medal_stanislav.name: Order of Stanislaus, 3rd Class
item.relic_medal_stanislav.desc: With swords and bow. Its owner never got to untie them. (Police post, locker)
item.relic_saber_cossack.name: Cossack Shashka, Zlatoust Mark
item.relic_saber_cossack.desc: Sharpened. Blade still greased: its owner meant to return. (Police post, arms rack)
item.relic_map_hand.name: Province Map, Hand-Drawn
item.relic_map_hand.desc: Watercolor roads, volosts; a child’s hand: “bears live here.” (School, teacher’s desk)
item.relic_gramota.name: Certificate “For Diligence”
item.relic_gramota.desc: Given to miller Startsev, 1912. Seal torn off — but by whom, and why? (School, cabinet)
item.relic_samovar_tula.name: Tula Samovar, Ornate
item.relic_samovar_tula.desc: Jubilee-shaped. The tap has a secret only one master knew. (Tavern, counter)
item.relic_harmon_chromka.name: Chromka Harmonica, Pearl
item.relic_harmon_chromka.desc: Frost-lumped bellows — the stove cures that. A broad Siberian voice. (Tavern, stage)
item.relic_axe_branded.name: Artel-Branded Axe
item.relic_axe_branded.desc: “Vetlugin Artel, 1915.” Three in the province; this is the best. (Sawmill, workbench)
item.relic_saw_frame.name: Cabinetmaker’s Bow Saw
item.relic_saw_frame.desc: Fine teeth for clean work. Whoever held it died a master. (Sawmill, shelf)
item.relic_ledger.name: Merchant's Ledger
item.relic_ledger.desc: Last quarter's debts and deeds of trust. Those who owe, owe no one now. (Shop, counter)
item.relic_scales.name: Apothecary Scales and Weights
item.relic_scales.desc: Accurate to a grain. Apothecary honesty in a tin case. (Feldsher's post)
item.relic_sygnum.name: Volost Seal
item.relic_sygnum.desc: Once bore two eagles. Now neither. Yet a seal remains a seal. (Volost office)
item.relic_camera.name: Tourist Camera
item.relic_camera.desc: Three plate holders. Plates fogged, the shutter snaps on briskly. (Dacha, attic)
item.relic_kerchief_scarce.name: Diagonal-Pattern Kerchief
item.relic_kerchief_scarce.desc: Given once in a lifetime. Smells of another's joy and mothballs. (Dacha, dresser)
item.relic_kamya.name: Seashell Cameo
item.relic_kamya.desc: A woman's profile, foreign work. How it got here — a district riddle. (Shop, floor cache)
item.relic_compass_legasy.name: Pilot's Compass
item.relic_compass_legasy.desc: The needle holds north, dead steady. North enough here for all. (Wharf, clerk's desk)
item.relic_ring_wedding.name: Wedding Ring, Triple-Band
item.relic_ring_wedding.desc: Three metals, three vows. Engraved inside: 'I. and M., until spring.' (Izba, chest)
item.relic_spinning.name: Carved Spinning Wheel
item.relic_spinning.desc: Blade carved with sun and horse. Spindle missing — perhaps for the best. (Well-off izba)
item.needle_sewing.name: Sewing Needle
item.needle_sewing.desc: A steel needle for mending clothes.
item.thimble.name: Thimble
item.thimble.desc: A copper thimble. Saves the finger.
item.scissors_tailor.name: Tailor's Shears
item.scissors_tailor.desc: Large, heavy, cuts through wool cloth.
item.file_steel.name: Steel File
item.tongs_smith.name: Smith's Tongs
item.hammer_locksmith.name: Locksmith's Hammer
item.plane_smooth.name: Smoothing Plane
item.chisel_wood.name: Chisel
item.hand_drill.name: Hand Drill
item.hand_drill.desc: A brace drill with a spare bit.
item.brace_bit.name: Carpenter's Brace
item.staple_iron.name: Iron Staple
item.crowbar_small.name: Pry Bar
item.axe_handle.name: Axe Handle
item.axe_handle.desc: Stout, cut from the butt of the log.
item.soldering_lamp.name: Soldering Lamp
item.soldering_lamp.desc: Heats and solders. Smells of kerosene.
item.trap_wolf.name: Wolf Trap
item.trap_wolf.desc: Steel jaws. Set it with mittens on.
item.trap_hare.name: Hare Trap
item.trap_hare.desc: A small trap for small game.
item.snare_loop.name: Snare Loop
item.snare_loop.desc: A wire loop on the hare's trail.
item.fish_vertushka.name: Wicker Fish Trap
item.net_fishing.name: Seine Net
item.net_fishing.desc: An old net. Heavy, but it catches.
item.rifle_sawnoff.name: Sawn-Off Rifle
item.rifle_sawnoff.desc: Double-barrelled sawn-off. A terror at close range.
item.ramrod.name: Ramrod
item.oil_can_gun.name: Gun Oil Can
item.gun_case.name: Gun Case
item.skis_hunting.name: Hunting Skis
item.skis_hunting.desc: Lined with reindeer hide — glides over snow like dry ground.
item.deer_call.name: Deer Call
item.deer_call.desc: A birch-bark tube. Calls the deer.
item.brush_marker.name: Badger-Hair Brush
item.brush_marker.desc: For marking trees and setting waymarks.
item.yoke.name: Shoulder Yoke
item.peel_oven.name: Oven Fork
item.peel_oven.desc: Holds the cast-iron pot in the stove.
item.pan_skillet.name: Skillet
item.pan_skillet.desc: Cast iron — it will outlive you.
item.samovar_brass.name: Copper Samovar
item.samovar_brass.desc: Fired with wood chips. The pride of the izba.
item.lamp_flashlight.name: Bat Lantern
item.glass_spare.name: Spare Lantern Glass
item.wicks_pack.name: Wicks
item.soap_lump.name: Household Soap
item.washboard.name: Washboard
item.iron_flat.name: Cast-Iron Flatiron
item.iron_flat.desc: Warms on the stove. At night — a bed warmer.
item.hot_water_bottle.name: Hot-Water Bottle
item.passport.name: Passport
item.passport.desc: Residence stamp inside. The owner won't be needing it back.
item.road_warrant.name: Road Warrant
item.mandat_red.name: Mandate
item.mandat_red.desc: Paper with a seal. Frightens better than a bayonet now.
item.gramota_church.name: Church Certificate
item.barometer_timofeich.name: Timofeich's Barometer
item.barometer_timofeich.desc: The needle trembles before a storm. It doesn't lie.
item.samovar_squeaky.name: Squeaky Samovar
item.samovar_squeaky.desc: It creaks, but it sings. Tea from it is medicine.
item.argunov_key.name: Argunov's Key
item.argunov_key.desc: Heavy, ornate. Opens the storehouse by the sawmill.
item.balalaika.name: Balalaika
item.balalaika.desc: Three strings, and all of Russia.
item.chess_set.name: Chess Set
item.chess_set.desc: Hand-carved, domovoi work. The bishop is worn bare.
item.dominoes.name: Dominoes
item.samogon_apparat.name: Moonshine Still
item.samogon_apparat.desc: A homemade coil. Keep it away from fire.
item.alpha_pelt.name: Pack Leader's Hat
item.alpha_pelt.desc: Sewn from the pack leader's hide, grey-streaked like a river blizzard. You'll not freeze.
item.bear_fang.name: Rogue Bear's Fang
item.bear_fang.desc: Finger-long, copper-set. Worn on the neck against evil death. Rogue bears never sleep.
item.treasure_map.name: Treasure Map
item.treasure_map.desc: The ataman's chewed pencil: three river bends, a dry aspen, a cross. No map, no gold.
